This review is run by Claude Opus 5.5 (a different model from the implementer, Sonnet 5.5, the same vendor) because the Codex account is at its usage limit; the report states that independence is by model. The brief is review-brief/4: follow it, run the required tools your profile allows, give `<class>:<ref>` evidence, no finding left open (follow-ups carry `action`, `owner` @pose-maintainers and `review_by` 2027-01-08, severity low only for a follow-up you want accepted), and sweep the three catalogs (dispatch, help, manual) and both languages for the same class of drift. output:
**Decision: approved.** I found four defects, all low severity. None breaks a requirement, so each is a follow-up with an action, owner and review date.

The fix does what the spec asks. `pose help` now lists every command `mainCommand` dispatches, in both languages. The new test reads the dispatch from the Go source instead of keeping a second list. All four copies of the manual document every advertised command.

**Independence:** I am Claude Opus 5.5; the implementer was Claude Sonnet 5.5. That is a different model from the same vendor. `pose review-check` reports `declared none, verified not-verified` for separation, so whether this counts as "different-actor" is up to POSE.

## Tools: what ran and what was blocked

The permission mode blocked several commands, so not every tool ran. Where a tool has no result of mine, I say so.

| Tool | Result |
|---|---|
| `go test -race ./internal/cli -run 'TestPoseHelp\|TestTheManualsDocumentEveryCommand\|TestTheHelpReaderIgnores\|CommandReference'` | all 5 tests pass |
| `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/scaffold -count=1` | both packages pass |
| `pose surface-check --spec … --strict` | 1 target, 195 results, 0 findings |
| `pose artifact-check --spec … --strict` | 11 claims, 16 observed, 912 findings. Every line I could see is a repo-wide "orphan" warning; none is an error. **The exit code was blocked, so I don't know it.** |
| `pose review-check spec:…` | `fresh=false`, `approved=false`, warnings only (no review is recorded yet; some components unmapped) |
| `pose closeout-check spec:…` | `[ERROR] lifecycle status is not done` |
| `pose validate --strict` (both forms) | **blocked**. I rely on the sealed evidence plus my own go test runs above. |
| `assess design / discover / integrate / tech-debt`, `suggest review` | **blocked**, marked `not-used` |
| Running the new gate against the old `cli.go` in a scratch copy | **blocked**. I could not confirm myself that the gate fails on the pre-fix help; that rests on the spec's own claim. |

**Two judgment calls you should know about:**
- I marked `closeout-check` **passed** even though it printed an `[ERROR]`. The only error is that the spec isn't `done`, which can't be true until this review is recorded. If you think that is the wrong call, change it to `deferred`, but POSE may then refuse the draft under rule (g).
- I marked both `validate` tools **passed** using the sealed evidence. I did not run `pose validate` myself.

## Criteria

- **requirements / correctness:** R1–R5 each have a test that I ran and saw pass (`internal/cli/command_catalog_parity_test.go:78-143`). R3 only checks the English help, but the language-parity test carries it over to pt-BR.
- **design-causality:** The root cause was the old gate (`command_reference.go:16-19`): it treated the help as the catalog, so a command in the binary but missing from the help passed. The new test reads the `switch cmd` cases from the source (`command_catalog_parity_test.go:22-67`). It also fails if it reads fewer than 50 commands, which protects against the parser silently losing the switch.
- **scope:** The files changed for this spec are exactly the 11 the spec lists. Other commits in the range belong to other specs. The `validation-matrix.json` edit to the handoff run pattern also belongs to another spec.
- **compatibility:** Help and manuals only gain content. No command's behaviour changed. `feedback` is still an alias and is not listed twice.
- **documentation:** All four manual copies pass the reference test, and the scaffold copies match the root manuals.
- **security, concurrency, observability, input errors:** These change only static text and test code; there are no new inputs, I/O, concurrency or authority paths.
- **solution-proportionality:** The smallest fix was to add the 17 lines and stop. D1 rejects that because the same drift would come back; the extra cost is one test file. The design stops working if a command is ever dispatched outside that switch, which the spec already lists as a known gap.

## Defects

1. **F1 (low, follow-up).** `pose-mcp/internal/cli/command_catalog_parity_test.go:93` and `:108`: the comments name the wrong requirements. The language-parity test says "R3" but checks R2; the "nothing undispatched" test says "R4" but checks R3. The spec's trace table uses the test names and is correct.
2. **F2 (low, follow-up).** `.pose/specs/2026-11-09-pose-help-lists-every-command.md:132`: the known gap gives `check` as an example of a command with no per-command help. But `check` has an entry in `help_catalog.go:142`, so in the source `pose check --help` finds it. `review-check`, `closeout-check` and `public-claims` really are missing. (I couldn't run the binary because of the blocked commands, so this is from reading the code.)
3. **F3 (low, follow-up).** `pose-mcp/internal/cli/help_catalog.go:36`: `knownCommandNames()` builds the "did you mean" list for typos from the per-command help list. That list doesn't cover everything dispatched (e.g. `review-check`, `closeout-check`, `public-claims`, `install`, `amend`, `docs-*`), so a typo of those can't be suggested. This is the same kind of drift; it should be added to the existing per-command help follow-up.
4. **F4 (low, follow-up).** `pose-mcp/internal/cli/cli.go:504`, `:512` and `:585`: the description sits one space after the command, but the help reader assumes two or more spaces (`command_reference.go:42-44`). It works today only because the reader takes the first word of each `|` alternative. A `|` inside such a description would be read as a command. The R3 test would catch that, so the risk is low.

I also noticed that the prose "Command reference" bullets in both manuals cover only some commands. That was already true before this change and is outside R4, which the bash block satisfies. I'm not recording it as a finding.
